answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil attacks by requiring every new identity to post a capped, non-transferable stake that is slashed when the identity is caught colluding with its own clones. Since the bond cannot be resold or pooled, each fake account carries its own ferrous lock-up of real value, so inflating a vote costs the attacker linearly rather than for free. Peers also trace endorsement history, so a swarm of fresh accounts with no umber of verified work is easy to spot, while an honest newcomer becomes a beacon that established agents vouch for.
